correctness.rationale: Hamming open-neighborhood centers u,v have shared neighbors only at center distances 1 or 2, giving the intersection geometry and uniqueness of a noncollinear triple center. Shattered pairs occur at distance one (d≥2,q≥3) or two (q≥3 or d≥3); shattered triples inside one N(c) partition by center-axis multiplicities 3,2+1,1+1+1, with sharp thresholds and combinatorial counts A, B, C. No four-set shattered: for a multi-axis four-set a three-subset has sole containing center c that also contains fourth; on one coordinate line no center produces an intermediate pair trace. Independent brute-force original-definition trace enumeration at seven parameter pairs reproduced s0..s3 and absence of quartets, including H(2,4) 320, H(3,3) 216, H(4,2) 64. All-parameter conclusion rests on proof.
residual_risks: Finite d,q brute-force checks are not an all-parameter or all-degree certificate; full no-quartet obstruction is essential.

value.rationale: A full shattering polynomial counts how many supports attain the VC threshold rather than only its existence; this is a natural combinatorial complexity invariant for Hamming graphs. The three geometrically distinct triple families, exact coefficients for all d,q and exceptional parameter thresholds remain genuinely informative beyond known dimension and the d=2 rook special case. It is a motivated complete classification.
residual_risks: The degree-bound part is already established; value rests on genuinely new coefficientwise counts for d≥3.

limitations: Full Hamming graphs d≥1,q≥2 and OPEN neighborhoods at distance one, not closed neighborhoods/other radii; prior d=2 exact rectangular rook special case and VCdim upper bound credited.
